variants: Basic, Venture, Pro and LIDAR versions on the product page, which list the same secondary-development row for all four and add obstacle avoidance and auto navigation as the version rises.
availability_note: DEEP Robotics' Lite3 shop page states a price, has a BUY NOW button, asks buyers to contact it before purchase and estimates shipping in 30 days, and its Delivery Policy says the product is delivered within 30 working days after the order is placed. Its purchase page also offers a purchase intention form that a consultant answers.

hardware.sensors: Front and rear obstacle stop and visual following on the Basic and Venture versions, forward obstacle avoidance added on the Pro version, and auto navigation added on the LIDAR version. Hardware interfaces run from two Ethernet ports on the Venture version to USB 3.0, HDMI, Ethernet and a power connector on the Pro and LIDAR versions.
hardware.actuation: The page says "50% joint torque increased" and lists a standing size of 610 x 370 x 406 mm, a weight of 12 kg with battery, a walking load of 5 kg, a 40-degree slope and an 18 cm stair for the Basic version. The Venture, Pro and LIDAR versions list loads of 4.5, 4 and 2.5 kg and weights of 12.2, 12.9 and 13.5 kg. The page lists no joint count.
hardware.power: A battery endurance of 1.5 to 2 hours and a mileage of 5 km on the Basic version, falling to 2.7 km on the LIDAR version. External power input of 24 V, 12 V and 5 V is listed on the Venture, Pro and LIDAR versions.

developer_access: DEEP Robotics' product page lists secondary development as "Provide models, motion control SDK and APIs, as well as perception development interfaces with sample code." Its rl_training repository "is a RL training library for deeprobotics robots, based on IsaacLab", lists the Lite3 among its environments, and says "If you want to deploy policies in mujoco or real robots, please use the corresponding deploy repo". Its Lite3_rl_deploy repository documents Sim-to-Sim and Sim-to-Real deployment to the Lite3 and says "To run the policy file trained with RL, you need to link the onnxruntime library, which supports models in the .onnx format." Its Lite3_MotionSDK repository documents the motion SDK and says Lite3_rl_deploy "is a implementation of rl on lite3 robot".
terms_note: DEEP Robotics' Lite3 shop page carries a Delivery Policy, an after-sales statement that the product does not support returns, and a warranty policy that starts when the buyer receives the goods; its Support page says the after-sales terms apply only in Chinese mainland. The Lite3_rl_deploy and rl_training repositories are released under the BSD 3-Clause License and the Lite3_MotionSDK repository under the MIT License.

terms_evidence.scope: Delivery, after-sales and warranty policy on the Lite3 shop page

not_verified: The documented policy interfaces are DEEP Robotics' own claims; the Atlas has not verified them. Every source is a DEEP Robotics web page or a file in a repository DEEP Robotics can change at any time.
